title: Why did this land in spam?
summary: A mail filter's rules, one email at a time, with the cutoff you can move.

inline.why: You've written to this address before.
Shouting subjects are a classic spam sign.
The domain was registered last month.
It answers an email you sent.
"paypa1" with a digit one, not an L.
A deadline to act on your account.
Asks you to sign in through a link.
You signed up for this digest.
Image-heavy mail scores a little higher.
Sent from a known bulk-mail network.
Your company has emailed this firm.
You bought from this shop once.

emails.sql: SELECT e.id, e.subject, e.sender, sum(s.points) AS score FROM emails e JOIN scores s ON s.email_id = e.id GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY score DESC

picked_rules.sql: SELECT rule, why, points, sum(points) OVER (ORDER BY points DESC, rule ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS running FROM scores WHERE email_id = $pick ORDER BY points DESC, rule

tally.sql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE score >= $cutoff) AS flagged, count(*) AS total FROM (SELECT email_id, sum(points) AS score FROM scores GROUP BY 1)
